stem:
Meera's class in Jaipur is discussing how science should really be learned. Her teacher says that science goes beyond the pages of the textbook.

Which of the following activities show learning science by observing, doing, and experimenting with the world around you?

1  Rohan reads the chapter on plants twice and memorises every definition without looking at a single real plant.
2  Asha observes the tulsi plant in her courtyard every morning and notes how its leaves turn towards sunlight.
3  Kabir copies the diagram of a water filter from the book neatly into his notebook without trying it out.
4  Priya mixes lemon juice with baking soda in her kitchen to see whether bubbles of gas are produced.

statements.text: Rohan reads the chapter on plants twice and memorises every definition without looking at a single real plant.
Asha observes the tulsi plant in her courtyard every morning and notes how its leaves turn towards sunlight.
Kabir copies the diagram of a water filter from the book neatly into his notebook without trying it out.
Priya mixes lemon juice with baking soda in her kitchen to see whether bubbles of gas are produced.

teacher.key_rationale: Only statements 2 and 4 involve learning science through observation and hands-on experimenting; statements 1 and 3 stay inside the book. Hence the correct set is 2 and 4, option C. Option A is the trap for a learner who counts statement 1 (pure reading/memorising) as genuine science learning, which the keyed set rejects.
